title: Oakridge Insights - integration call capture
content:
Attendees: Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood infra), Priya (solutions), Sam (Oakridge engineering), Jen K. (Oakridge product), Tom L. (Oakridge infra)

Objective: quick scoping call to capture Oakridge Insights' integration constraints and priorities for a Private (VPC) deployment pilot. They want a small initial pilot (1 model / 2 endpoints) for summarization + reranking on PII-marked support transcripts.

Background notes: Oakridge is a mid-market analytics vendor that processes customer support transcripts (speech->text pipeline already in place). They need Redwood to host inference inside their AWS account (VPC endpoints) due to PII and retention policies. They estimate 2000 daily conversations, bursty traffic during 09:00-18:00 PST with spikes up to 20 RPS for short periods. Latency SLO for 95th percentile: < 250ms for summaries, < 150ms for reranker (they prefer lower but will tolerate slightly higher for first phase).

Key requirements (captured verbatim / prioritized):
- Private control plane in Oakridge VPC; no transcript text leaves VPC (must confirm whether control plane metadata is allowed).
- KMS integration for key management (AES-256 + HSM preferred)
- Audit logs exported to their Splunk instance for every inference call (token counts, model id, latency)
- Model pinning: ability to pin to a specific model SHA/variant during pilot, and can opt into auto-updates later
- Per-route backpressure/fallback: reranker must have a cheap fallback (lexical baseline) when model capacity is exhausted
- Minimal changes to existing auth: prefer using their existing OIDC provider and SAML for console access

Non-functional constraints / capacity:
- Baseline QPS planning: steady-state 3 RPS, expected peaks up to 20 RPS. Burst tolerance needed for ~2 min windows.
- Average prompt length: 450 tokens (after speech normalization) for summarization; reranker queries ~80 tokens.
- Expected average response tokens: summary 150 tokens, reranker 32 tokens.
- Cost sensitivity: Oakridge wants a cost estimate for 50k generated tokens/day and 100k embed/rerank units/month.

Gotchas / flags (from call):
- PII scrubbing: Oakridge does initial PII redaction upstream, but their security team insists Redwood must support in-flight redaction or at least a token-level obfuscation option.
- Network egress: Their procurement asked about whether any telemetry is sent outside VPC; we need to provide a diagram of control vs data plane flows.
- Character encoding: some transcripts contain special proprietary markers (\u201C<<CUST_TAG:…>>\u201D). Need to ensure tokenization doesn’t mangle tags they use for entity linking.
- Cold-start latency: they run intermittent jobs overnight; concerned about first-request p95 when autoscaler has scaled down. Consider warm-pools or scheduled keep-alive.
- Compliance: they asked whether audit logs meet SOC2 audit formats; if not, what mappings are available.

Prototype approach (recommended during call):
1) Start with an internal sandbox in their VPC using Redwood Private with a small dedicated node pool (1-2 GPUs) to validate performance and audit logging.
2) Use a quantized model variant for reranker (higher throughput) and a higher-precision variant for summarization.
3) Add prefix/KV caching for summarization to reuse repeated preambles (many transcripts have same system prompts).
4) Implement a lexical fallback in the client side (simple TF-IDF rerank) wired to Redwood fallback policy.

Immediate action items (owners & rough due dates):
- Maya: draft architecture diagram (control vs data plane) and share by 2024-05-24. Action: include telemetry fields and confirm which fields are considered metadata vs PII. (Jira SE-4123)
- Diego: confirm options for KMS/HSM integration and whether we can use customer-managed keys in their AWS account. Due 2024-05-27. (Jira INF-2211)
- Priya: prepare cost estimate for pilot scenarios: steady-state and 3x burst. Due 2024-05-26. (Jira PRT-998)
- Sam (Oakridge): send sample sanitized transcript (10 examples) and a representative high-entropy transcript with proprietary tags by 2024-05-23.
- Jen (Oakridge product): confirm retention policy (how long transcripts must be kept) and legal contact for SOC2 questions by 2024-05-25.

Open questions to resolve:
- Does Oakridge require that even control-plane metadata never leaves their VPC? (They said "prefer", but need specifics).
- Are we comfortable offering in-flight redaction as an optional preprocess? Scope and cost impact?
- Which Splunk ingestion format do they expect? (raw JSON event per call vs batched logs)

Notes to self / quick reminders:
- Follow-up: arrange short tech deep-dive with our Private deploy PM + infra lead after they share transcripts.
- Consider creating a small demo using our dedupe + prefix cache to show 2x token savings for repeated support headers.
- Prototype can initially use hosted model weights mirrored into their VPC storage but confirm licensing.

Reference links / snippets we promised to send:
- Redwood Private quickstart (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIVATE/Quickstart
- Sample audit log schema (internal): attached example -> SE-4123

End notes (informal):
- Oakridge seemed pragmatic; main blocker is procurement / legal on SOC2 + KMS. Product folks excited about low-latency reranker (they benchmarked LexRank prepilot).
- Keep cost estimates explicit (per-token and per-hour GPU) so procurement can compare to building in-house.

-- Maya
